# DuckDB product mapping for the pinned Triplex value contract

3 November 2026. Source analysis and hand derivation only. This does not select an adapter implementation, capability subset or executable action.

## The boundaries must remain separate

Triplex's tagged storage value is not its public Datalog scalar. At the pinned source revision, storage has string, number, boolean, datetime, ref, JSON and blob families. Typed storage reads reconstruct those tags and blob metadata. Datalog constants, joins, predicates, projection, grouping and ordering have a different scalar-family contract. A future adapter must preserve both boundaries rather than pass the native prototype's values through unchanged. Sources: [Triplex value declarations](https://github.com/bjacobso/triplex/blob/e24dcdbfce4e61da3e2f08c0e4f2a4531c7df0a0/packages/core/src/Value.ts#L4-L79), [typed row reconstruction](https://github.com/bjacobso/triplex/blob/e24dcdbfce4e61da3e2f08c0e4f2a4531c7df0a0/packages/core/src/store/TriplesLive.ts#L77-L111), and [public scalar compiler](https://github.com/bjacobso/triplex/blob/e24dcdbfce4e61da3e2f08c0e4f2a4531c7df0a0/packages/core/src/datalog/compiler.ts#L273-L407).

The current prototype deliberately has four disjoint tags: string, boolean, int64 and finite float64. This is the accepted product contract, not a defect. The native `Value` equality rejects cross-tag equality; its dictionary has separate integer and float maps. Its string order is UTF-8 byte order and its global value order is tag rank. Sources: [typed core header]([PRIVATE_REFERENCE_REMOVED]), [core equality and ordering]([PRIVATE_REFERENCE_REMOVED]), [typed dictionary]([PRIVATE_REFERENCE_REMOVED]).

## Representation map and unselected choices

| Triplex boundary | Current product source | Requirement for a future selected subset |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Stored string | String tag, UTF-8 scalar text, no NUL; persisted E/A/value text capped at 512 UTF-8 bytes | Retain the product's guards. State narrower limits as unsupported inputs rather than truncating or claiming the full Triplex string domain. |
| Stored boolean | Exact Boolean tag and exact Python bool admission | Preserve bool versus number; do not use Python's bool/int subtype relationship as a conversion rule. |
| Stored number | Separate int64 and finite float64 tags; exact i64 decimal-string wire | Choose an explicit JavaScript-number boundary. Splitting integral values into i64 and fractional values into f64 can introduce native cross-tag distinctions that Triplex does not have. |
| Stored datetime | No datetime value tag | Keep a storage-tag distinction from number if this family is claimed, even though Datalog flattens both to a numeric scalar. A float or integer alone cannot retain which stored family was used. |
| Stored ref | No ref value tag | Preserve tag-exact typed storage reads and typed-ref pattern matching, while honoring flattened text-family query behavior. A plain native string alone does not retain both contracts. |
| Stored JSON | No JSON value tag or object payload | Define a separate storage codec and the pinned serialized-text query behavior if claimed. Do not equate the content-hash canonical encoder with the plain JSON.stringify path used here. |
| Stored blob | No blob tag or MIME/size/filename fields | A hash string alone loses storage metadata. The query scalar and typed storage object must remain distinct. |
| Query result null from optional projection or empty non-count aggregation | No native null value tag | This null is a query result state, not a new stored TripleValue tag. Stored JSON can separately contain a null payload. Supporting result null requires an explicit outer representation. |

The schema2 product's selected five-field STRUCT carrier admits exactly one non-null payload under its tag. Schema SQL enforces four tags, finite DOUBLE values, half-open int64 valid intervals and logical position intervals. None of these checks supplies a Triplex service or its seven storage-tag contract. Sources: [schema2]([PRIVATE_REFERENCE_REMOVED]), [carrier and public codec]([PRIVATE_REFERENCE_REMOVED]), [Value identity and wire]([PRIVATE_REFERENCE_REMOVED]).

These are design obligations, not a claim that an adapter is impossible. An additional facade or storage representation could preserve the distinctions, but no such choice or implementation is selected here.

## Numeric precision and time are different contracts

The product's JSON i64 codec requires a canonical signed decimal string and emits the exact integer as a string. Triplex's number/datetime helpers and schema use JavaScript numbers. A decimal-string-to-Number conversion can therefore lose an exact product integer. For example, the int64 integer 9,007,199,254,740,993 is between adjacent representable binary64 integers and cannot survive that conversion as itself. The exact product wire must not be relabeled as lossless Triplex numeric support. The numeric hand derivation follows the [ECMAScript Number representation](https://tc39.es/ecma262/multipage/ecmascript-data-types-and-values.html#sec-ecmascript-language-types-number-type) and [safe-integer distinction](https://tc39.es/ecma262/multipage/numbers-and-dates.html#sec-number.max_safe_integer).

A safe-integer bound is a possible conservative policy, not the only mathematical round-trip criterion for values: some larger even integers are exactly representable. The future contract must decide what it accepts and how it reports a boundary violation. It must not silently change the value to a string, because a string belongs to a different query family. No policy is selected by this research.

Triplex public read-basis instants resolved through `resolveTemporalBasis` are checked as finite, nonnegative epoch-millisecond numbers. The inspected resolver does not require an integer. Its public `validAt: 0.5` is therefore within that resolver's arithmetic condition, whereas the current product query cut requires an exact signed int64. Silently truncating or rounding the cut changes temporal visibility. Conversely, the product's negative int64 time domain is not proof that Triplex accepts negative public read-basis time. Pagination adds a distinct safe-integer rule for the recorded commit position. Do not apply a single numeric conversion policy indiscriminately to value payloads, temporal instants, commit positions and aggregate results. Sources: [Triplex time resolver](https://github.com/bjacobso/triplex/blob/e24dcdbfce4e61da3e2f08c0e4f2a4531c7df0a0/packages/core/src/Temporal.ts#L24-L45), [pagination cut validation](https://github.com/bjacobso/triplex/blob/e24dcdbfce4e61da3e2f08c0e4f2a4531c7df0a0/packages/core/src/Pagination.ts#L176-L212), [product query snapshot]([PRIVATE_REFERENCE_REMOVED]).

## Equality, ordering and aggregates need translation

The product allows ordered comparison of same-tag strings and rejects mixed-tag ordered comparisons. Triplex's ordinary Datalog predicates instead restrict ordered comparison to its numeric family and flatten number/datetime together. A translator cannot accept every native comparison as an equivalent Triplex query or translate a Triplex number using whichever native numeric tag appears convenient. Sources: [native comparisons]([PRIVATE_REFERENCE_REMOVED]), [Triplex query schema](https://github.com/bjacobso/triplex/blob/e24dcdbfce4e61da3e2f08c0e4f2a4531c7df0a0/packages/core/src/datalog/schema.ts#L101-L107).

Native aggregate count consumes the completed set of full source tuples, retaining distinct witnesses that project the same measure. Native sum_i64 requires int64 measures, while min/max reject booleans and mixed measure tags; avg is not a native aggregate kind. Triplex COUNT(?value) is distinct over flattened public source scalars, and its other aggregate contract must be mapped separately. A two-witness same-measure product count is therefore not automatically Triplex COUNT(?value). Empty global native sum_i64 yields int64 zero and native min/max yield no tuple; the pinned Triplex source assertions instead expect null for empty sum/avg/min/max and zero for count. This is an intentional contract difference, not evidence that either implementation failed. Sources: [native aggregate completion]([PRIVATE_REFERENCE_REMOVED]), [Triplex source assertions](https://github.com/bjacobso/triplex/blob/e24dcdbfce4e61da3e2f08c0e4f2a4531c7df0a0/packages/testkit/src/index.ts#L1218-L1267).

Ordering also has a concrete boundary. The native rank starts string, boolean, int64, float64. The pinned KV public scalar comparator ranks numeric, boolean, text, null and compares strings using JavaScript `<`. Native UTF-8 ordering is not interchangeable with that UTF-16 code-unit order for all Unicode. The hand control comparing U+E000 with U+10000 separates them. The inspected SQL query paths do not establish cross-dialect Unicode collation parity, so this research does not claim a universal Triplex Unicode order. Sources: [KV comparator](https://github.com/bjacobso/triplex/blob/e24dcdbfce4e61da3e2f08c0e4f2a4531c7df0a0/packages/core/src/kv/datalog/executor.ts#L647-L675), [ECMAScript string comparison](https://tc39.es/ecma262/multipage/abstract-operations.html#sec-islessthan).

Any later code or executable checks require separate selection and applicable gates. This source-only map releases no hold and grants no retry.
